component.name: Lob
component.summary: Choose which browser opens each link
Auswählen, welcher Browser welchen Link öffnet
Choisir quel navigateur ouvre chaque lien
Scegli quale browser apre ciascun collegamento

description.p: Lob registers as the system handler for http and https links and decides where each one should go, instead of sending everything to a single default browser.

Links that match a rule open straight away, after a brief bar that can be interrupted to choose something else. Anything unrecognised shows a keyboard-driven picker listing installed browsers and their profiles, with an option to remember the choice for that host.
Lob handles http and https only. It does not claim mail links, local files or PDFs.
Lob registriert sich als Systemzuordnung für http- und https-Links und entscheidet für jeden einzeln, wohin er gehen soll, statt alles an einen einzigen Standardbrowser zu schicken.

Links, auf die eine Regel zutrifft, werden sofort geöffnet – nach einem kurzen Balken, der sich unterbrechen lässt, um etwas anderes zu wählen. Alles Unbekannte zeigt eine tastaturbediente Auswahl der installierten Browser und ihrer Profile, mit der Möglichkeit, die Wahl für diesen Host zu merken.
Lob verarbeitet ausschließlich http und https. E-Mail-Links, lokale Dateien und PDFs beansprucht es nicht.
Lob s'enregistre comme gestionnaire système des liens http et https et décide pour chacun où il doit aller, au lieu de tout envoyer vers un unique navigateur par défaut.

Les liens correspondant à une règle s'ouvrent immédiatement, après une brève barre que l'on peut interrompre pour choisir autre chose. Tout ce qui n'est pas reconnu affiche un sélecteur pilotable au clavier listant les navigateurs installés et leurs profils, avec la possibilité de mémoriser le choix pour cet hôte.
Lob ne traite que http et https. Il ne revendique ni les liens de courriel, ni les fichiers locaux, ni les PDF.
Lob si registra come gestore di sistema per i collegamenti http e https e decide per ciascuno dove debba andare, invece di inviare tutto a un unico browser predefinito.

I collegamenti che corrispondono a una regola si aprono subito, dopo una breve barra che si può interrompere per scegliere altro. Tutto ciò che non viene riconosciuto mostra un selettore utilizzabile da tastiera con l'elenco dei browser installati e dei loro profili, con la possibilità di memorizzare la scelta per quell'host.
Lob gestisce soltanto http e https. Non rivendica i collegamenti di posta, i file locali o i PDF.

description.p: A release of fixes, most of all to focus.

ul.li: A link a rule or a remembered choice decides now brings the browser to the front. Through the hold bar it mostly opened behind whatever was already there.
The match and action dropdowns in the settings window edit the rule they belong to, rather than whichever rule shared the option's number.
Remembering a path covers that path segment and no other: github.com/kde no longer answers for github.com/kdeconnect.
A shortened link inside a link scanner still opens through the scanner once the shortener is resolved.
A hold as long as the maximum no longer drops the link.
Applications whose names merely contain a browser's, such as "Operator", are no longer mistaken for browsers.

description.p: Lob can be configured without a text editor, and speaks three more languages.

ul.li: A settings window over the rules, the remembered choices, the applications that register for links without being browsers, and the hold duration. Rules are listed in the order they are matched and can be reordered there, because that order decides which one wins.
"Remember" can now cover a host, a whole domain, or everything under a path, rather than always the host alone. "lob --forget" drops whichever memory actually decides a link.
The picker can be filtered by typing, which it needed once a machine had more browsers and profiles than there are digits.
German, Italian and French. None of the three has been reviewed by a native speaker yet, and corrections are welcome.

description.p: Lob looks like itself now, and installs somewhere other than Arch.

ul.li: An icon of its own. Lob no longer borrows the generic web-browser icon, which made the application for telling browsers apart the one you could not tell apart.

A remembered choice can be undone. "Remember for this host" had no way back short of editing rules.json by hand; "lob --forget <host>" drops it, and "lob --explain" names the command when a memory is what decided a link.
Lob can be translated. Every string is in one catalogue and a translation is installed and used once someone writes one. None ships yet, so English is still what you get.
A Fedora package, built and installed on every change.
A rule that could never match is refused rather than accepted. A pathPrefix pattern with no path matched nothing and said nothing about it; it is now reported when the file is read.
Without layer-shell, the picker opens on the screen the pointer is on rather than wherever it was last shown.

description.p: Links now reach the browser you meant, and say so when they cannot.

ul.li: A link clicked in Slack, a search result or a mail client is routed by where it actually goes, rather than by the redirector it arrived through.
The picker stays up until a launch succeeds or fails, and a choice is remembered only once it has worked.
Desktop entries are honoured as written, so Flatpak browsers, wrapped commands and custom profile directories launch correctly.
Private windows never silently fall back to ordinary ones.
Every browser profile keeps a stable identity, and the picker no longer lists the same browser twice.
A malformed or half-finished edit to rules.json leaves the last valid configuration in place instead of dropping every rule.
Restoring the previous default browser puts back exactly what was there, including having had no default at all.
A URL copied to the clipboard survives the process that copied it.

description.p: First working version: browser and profile discovery, a keyboard-driven picker, rules with a hold bar, and a resident daemon.
